title: A list_item url action runs with no record in context: ${ctx.recordId}, ${ctx.record.id} and ${ctx.selection.ids} interpolate to empty in a row menu
body:
Found by objectstack-ai/duly#113 (PR duly#175) on @objectstack 18.2.0, measured in a live console.

## What happens

duly declares a `type: 'url'` action on `sys_user`:

```ts
defineAction({
  name: 'duly_member_open',
  objectName: 'sys_user',
  type: 'url',
  target: '/apps/ai.objectstack.duly/sys_user/record/${ctx.recordId}/page/duly_member',
  locations: ['list_item', 'record_header'],
})
```

- In `record_header` (the record's "⋯" menu) it works: `${ctx.recordId}` is the record's id, and the click lands on the right route.
- In `list_item` (the row menu of a list view) the action renders, but the click lands on `/apps/ai.objectstack.duly/sys_user/record/page/duly_member`. `${ctx.recordId}`, `${ctx.record.id}` and `${ctx.selection.ids}` all interpolate to empty.

The spec documents `ctx.recordId` for url actions, and a row is a record context, so the row menu should carry the row's record the way the header does.

## Expected

A `list_item` url action interpolates `${ctx.recordId}` (and `${ctx.record.*}`) from the row it was opened on.

## Workaround in the app

duly ships the action at `record_header` only, and pins the location with a note to re-measure before adding `list_item` back.
